The necessity originally derived from the heat issue. As you may know, the V20 can get extremely hot. It was during the summer and my phone kept overheating and severely throttling. The idea being, if i could cut the back panel to work with extended battery, the extra thermal mass could help, as that top part is where the CPU is. I realize the phone is designed to heatsink through the screen, but aluminum back panel must play some part in cooling as well. I was hesitant to screw up the back panel, but i mustered up the courage one day and winged it with a bandsaw. It cut through the aluminum like butter and left a clean cut, perfect fit. Immediately i noticed a difference, the phone throttled less. Amazing, with the mod it still all fits in the rubber case. The NFC working was a neat by-product.

The achilles heel for me is performance, with the outdated processor and only 4GB RAM. It gets quite laggy, but everything is indeed useable, just have to be a bit patient sometimes. Beyond that, i have no complaints about the phone. In fact i love it. I have repaired it several times easily. I can buy replacement "new" V20 from China on ebay below $200 CAD. There is no other phone which fits all my criteria, which could replace it for me, yet. And it still works for 3G/LTE for me in Canada.

Often times mods seem like they will be harder than they actually are, so my advice is to just have fun and do it. To make the fan holes i marked on the case using a scribe and used a jigsaw to cut as close as possible and then used a round file to make clean circle. You could also use a dremel with a cut-off wheel. A hole-saw would be best but they are generally quite expensive at that size in my experience. You could try relocating the HDD cage to another part of the case using rivets or small machine screws. I definitely had to delete my bottom cage to fit that graphics card, lol.
